sections.intro: Read “Combing” and answer questions 11–14. The vocabulary note follows the poem.

questions.prompt: As used in the first stanza, the words “bending,” “bow,” and “lay my hands” help establish

choices.text: a simple amusement women share to pass the time
a tedious routine with which women must help one another
the power struggle between women of different ages
the shared respect women bestow upon one another

questions.explanation: The speaker bends and bows while gently laying her hands on her daughter’s hair. Those almost ceremonial gestures frame combing as a caring, respectful act shared among the women, not a chore or contest.

questions.prompt: The phrase “I take her place” (line 10) reflects a shift in
questions.explanation: In the first stanza, the speaker is combing her daughter’s hair. At line 10, she remembers being the child under her own mother’s hands, so the poem moves from the present to an earlier time.

questions.prompt: As used in line 29, the word “plaiting” most nearly means
questions.explanation: To plait hair is to braid strands together. The final line uses that action figuratively: the shared hair-care ritual intertwines the lives of daughter, mother, and grandmother across generations.

questions.explanation: Each stanza connects a similar scene across generations: the speaker combs her daughter’s hair, remembers her mother combing hers, and recalls a grandmother’s hair being combed. These parallel acts build the poem’s theme.
